$comment: The scope of gate-case-counts.sh, kept OUT of the gate so that adding a document to the sweep is a data change a reviewer can see in a diff, not a literal buried mid-script. Measured 2026-09-11 on this tree: docs/gate-requirements.md cites 23 case counts of the form `N cases` beside the name of a battery, docs/competitive-analysis.md cites 3 more, and nothing executed any of them. In iteration 4 four of those figures went false on a single branch and a fifth expired across two, which is the shape of drift this file exists to end.
$comment_docs: Paths relative to the repository root. A document listed here and absent from disk is exit 2, never a pass: a sweep that quietly skips its own scope is the false green this gate was written against.
$comment_ceiling: A RATCHET, and the half of this gate that stops approval-by-omission. A citation `(N cases)` carrying no `<!-- cases: PATH -->` marker is invisible to the comparison, so an author could add a figure nobody measures and the gate would stay green. It cannot: unmarked citations are counted and compared against this number, and MORE unmarked citations than declared is exit 1.
$comment_why_a_tolerance_at_all: Because eight of the twenty-six citations cannot be marked today, and a gate that demands the impossible gets deleted rather than satisfied. Measured 2026-09-11, one by one: (a) FOUR citations - gate-requirements.md lines 29, 30, 32 and 44 - name gates whose self-test is inline and prints NO total at all (gate-agent-roster.sh, gate-stage-eval-floor.sh, gate-coverage-gap-claims.sh, gate-negative-proof-census.sh; the last does not even accept --self-test). There is no summary line to read, so marking them would pin them at exit 2 forever. The fix is in those four gates - have their self-test print a total - and it is not this gate's to make. (b) ONE citation - line 80, `59 cases` - is an AGGREGATE of the four batteries summed in the table above it, and a marker names one battery. The four ROWS of that table are each marked, so the four addends are measured even though their sum is not; a sum that stops matching its own addends is the one hole this gate leaves open, and it is named here rather than left to be found. (c) THREE citations in competitive-analysis.md (lines 677 twice and 784) count dataset rows and bench cases, not battery cases; there is no battery to run.
$comment_ratchet_only_goes_down: This number goes DOWN when one of those eight becomes measurable, and never up. Raising it is how the hole reopens, so a pull request that raises it is asking a reviewer to approve a figure nobody measures - state the reason here, in this file, where the diff shows it.
$comment_the_cases_now_column: The four counts in the table at gate-requirements.md lines 73-76 are case counts in a column called `Cases now`, written as BARE INTEGERS rather than as `N cases`. They match no citation pattern, so the ratchet above never counted them and nothing measured them - and one of them was already false: measured 2026-09-11, `gate-plugin-integrity.selftest.sh` prints 22, not the 20 that column claimed. They are closed rather than documented: the marker reads the LAST INTEGER before it on the line, which a table cell satisfies without any `N cases` wording, so each of the four rows now carries a marker. Two cases in the battery prove that claim instead of asserting it - a bare integer in a table cell agreeing, and the same cell off by one going red. Note what this does NOT change: those four never matched the citation pattern, so they were never in the unmarked count, and the ceiling above therefore stays at 8 rather than moving. A ceiling that rose here would have been a mistake.
